subject.title: fix(linux): harden Quick Chat widget lifecycle

question: Should this protected Linux lifecycle change merge after the current test/build evidence, or should it require a real Quick Chat behavior capture for the reconnect and visibility-race paths first?
rationale: The branch changes native WebView lifecycle ordering and retry behavior; automated tests validate important contracts, but the supplied evidence does not observe the user-facing Linux sequence that the patch is intended to stabilize.

options.title: Require live Linux proof
options.body: Request a redacted terminal log, recording, or screenshot-backed run that exercises widget visibility across reload/reconnect and transient refresh recovery before merge.

options.title: Accept focused automated proof
options.body: Explicitly accept the current Rust, Vitest, build, and CI evidence as sufficient for this protected lifecycle follow-up.

recommendation.title: Require live Linux proof
recommendation.body: Request a redacted terminal log, recording, or screenshot-backed run that exercises widget visibility across reload/reconnect and transient refresh recovery before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the prior merged widget implementation and the proposed lifecycle model.
